claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask about Alex's current situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's current activities.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?** If so, when did he leave education, and when did he register?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just finished school and is taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have just one more question to complete my assessment.

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just at home trying to work out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me, let me provide my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Result: Unfortunately, you are INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For young people aged 16-19, you can still qualify if they remain in approved education or training. 

Since Alex is 18 and is not currently:
- In approved education or training
- Registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Working 24 hours or more per week

He does not meet the criteria for extended Child Benefit eligibility beyond age 16.

**However, there may be options for Alex:** If he decides to return to education or start an approved training program in the future, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again at that point, as long as he's under 20 when he starts. If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Additionally, the rules allow Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Alex is 18 years old and has not registered with either a careers service or the armed services. He is not working 24 hours or more per week, and he is not in approved education or training. Therefore, based on the eligibility criteria provided, Alex does not meet the requirements for Child Benefit as he is over 16, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or armed services (and even if he had, he is beyond the 16-17 age range for that exception).
